info.title: Shipdok API
info.description:
The API behind the Shipdok dashboard. Everything the dashboard does goes through it.

**Signing in.** Sign in with `POST /api/auth/login`; the answer sets the cookie `shipdok.sid`, which every other call needs (except the ones marked as open). Sessions end after 30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all.

**State-changing calls and the `Origin` header.** A browser sends `Origin` itself and it must be one of Shipdok's own addresses (the address the dashboard is opened at, or the configured public address). A call with no `Origin` header at all (for example `curl`) is accepted, so scripts only need the cookie.

**Who can reach it.** Visitors from outside the local network get a plain `404 {"error":"Not found"}` for everything in `local` mode, and for everything except `POST /api/webhooks/github` in `webhook` mode (see the Security page's Public access).

**Errors** are JSON: `{"error": "a sentence"}`, with `code` (a short stable code) and `details` where there are any.

**Asynchronous work.** Deploying, rolling back, starting, stopping, restarting, cleaning up and deleting are queued for the worker and answer **202**; follow the result in the app's `runtime`, the deployment's `status` or `GET /api/apps/{id}`.

delete.description: Deletes the app: its containers, images, logs, variables and every deployment record. **Its persistent volumes are kept by default**; send `deleteVolumes: true` to remove them and their data too. The API only marks the app and queues the work; the worker does it (so the answer is 202, and the app disappears when the worker has finished; a failure shows as `delete_error`, and sending the delete again retries). **The exact name must be sent as `confirm`.** Refused while a deployment is queued or running.

400.description: The confirmation does not match (`code: confirm_mismatch`), or `deleteVolumes` is not true or false.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

409.description: A deployment is still running; cancel it first (`code: deployment_active`).

503.description: The job queue is not available.

deleteVolumes.description: Also delete the app's persistent volumes and their data, permanently. Default `false`: the data is kept (the volumes become orphaned and stay listed under `GET /api/volumes`).

get.description: The app as the dashboard shows it, plus `settings_pending`: which edited settings the running version does not have yet.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

put.description: Changes the settings you send. **Nothing running is touched:** the next deployment uses the new values (see `settings_pending`, which includes the build time limit); the name and the restart limit apply at once. The repository and the slug cannot be changed (delete the app and create a new one). The GitHub App (`github_app_id`) can: it is read when a deployment starts and when a push arrives, so it is **not** a pending change; the installation is looked up again with the new app and a `warning` says if it is not installed on the repository.

400.description: Invalid settings (`details`).

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

409.description: The name or host port belongs to another app (`code: name_taken` or `port_taken`, and `app` names it), or the app is being deleted.

delete.description: Removes it. The running app keeps its copy until the next deployment.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The variable's name: letters, digits and underscore, not starting with a digit, at most 128 characters; some names are reserved.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

put.description: Stores the value encrypted (AES-256-GCM, bound to the app and the name). The running app keeps its old value until the next deployment. `scope` says where the variable is available: `runtime` (the container; the default for a new variable), `build` (only `docker build --build-arg`; the container never sees it) or `both`. `buildAs` says how a variable that reaches the build is given to `docker build`: `arg` (a build argument, the default; the Dockerfile declares it with `ARG NAME`, and if it uses it the value is stored in the image) or `secret` (a BuildKit secret, `--secret id=NAME,env=NAME`; the Dockerfile asks for it with `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=NAME,env=NAME ...`; the value is mounted for that step only and never stored in the image, and a changed secret does not re-run a cached step). Send a `value`, a `scope`, a `buildAs`, a `newKey`, or any of them together: a value alone keeps the scope and `buildAs`; a scope or `buildAs` alone changes an existing variable and keeps its value (404 if there is no such variable). `newKey` renames an existing variable (the value is encrypted for its name, so the server decrypts and encrypts it again, in the same transaction as the rest of the request; the value never leaves the server). The new name follows the same rules as any name, 409 `name_taken` if another variable has it, and the answer says `previous_key`. Until the next deployment the old name counts as removed and the new one as added. A build variable is baked into the image if the Dockerfile uses it (`ARG NAME`), so use it for public configuration, not secrets; some names (`PATH`, `HOME`, `DOCKER_*`, `BUILDKIT_*`, `LD_*`...) cannot be used at build time.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The variable's name: letters, digits and underscore, not starting with a digit, at most 128 characters; some names are reserved.

previous_key.description: Only after a rename: the name it had.

500.description: A rename of a stored value that cannot be decrypted (has `APP_SECRETS_KEY` changed?); send a new value with it.

value.description: The value; at most 64 KB, no null characters. Leave it out to change only the scope or `buildAs`.

scope.description: Where the variable is available. Default for a new variable: `runtime`; an existing variable keeps its scope when this is left out.

buildAs.description: How a variable that reaches the build is given to `docker build`. Default for a new variable: `arg`; an existing variable keeps what it has when this is left out.

newKey.description: Rename the variable to this name (it must already exist, and the new name must be free).

delete.description: Deletes both the current and the previous run's log. Refused while the app's output is still being collected (stop the app first).

delete.description: Forgets that app. The projects assigned to it keep running and are left with **no GitHub app and no remembered installation**: private repositories cannot be built, and pushes do not deploy them, until they are given another GitHub app in their settings. The dashboard lists those projects (`projects` in `GET /api/github`) before asking. Shipdok cannot delete the app on github.com. Needs the current password.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of a connected GitHub App (from `GET /api/github`).

delete.summary: Dismiss the notice about a refused push
delete.description: Forgets what was recorded (in memory) about refused pushes from that sender, so the warning on the GitHub page goes away. Nothing is deployed or changed; the next refused push from the same sender brings the warning back. Answers 204 whether or not there was anything recorded.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: GitHub's number for the app that sent the push (digits, as `appNumber` in `unknownSenders` and the App ID of a connected app), or `none` for a push that did not say which app sent it.

delete.summary: Delete a volume and its data, for good
delete.description: **Permanent.** Only a volume that is not mounted by an app. The API only queues it; the worker removes the Docker volume (and refuses one that is not Shipdok's or that a container still uses; the reason then shows as `removeError` on the volume).

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

409.description: The volume is mounted by an app (`code: volume_in_use`).

get.summary: May this visitor see the dashboard?
get.description: Used by the dashboard's web server before it serves a page: **204** for a local visitor or when the mode is `full`, otherwise **403**. Not for general use.

204.description: The visitor may see the dashboard.

403.description: The visitor may not (the web server turns this into a 404).

get.description: Every app, newest first, each with its newest deployment, what the worker last reported (`runtime`), the last image clean-up, the settings the running version was deployed with (`running_settings`) and the latest CPU and memory reading (`stats`, `null` when stale).

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

post.description: Registers an app; nothing is built until you deploy. Leave `host_port` out and the lowest free port in the platform's port range (default 20000-20999) is used. Choose the GitHub App the project uses with `github_app_id` (one of `GET /api/github`; `null` or left out: none, which is fine for a public repository). The API then looks up that app's installation for the repository; a missing installation never blocks creation and only adds a `warning` (public repositories still deploy).

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

409.description: The name or host port is taken (the message says which), or every port in the range is used (`code: no_free_port`).

get.summary: Why the app was not running
get.description: The last 20 times the app was not running when it should have been, newest first, with what Shipdok did about each: crash, stopped outside Shipdok, recovered after a host restart, or container removed outside Shipdok.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

post.description: Queues a build and deployment of the branch's latest commit. Older queued or running deployments of the app are superseded (the newest wins). Answers 202 at once; follow the deployment with `GET /api/deployments/{id}`. Send `noCache: true` to build this one deployment without Docker's build cache. Under 10% free disk the request is refused (409 `disk_critical`) unless the body says `ignoreDiskWarning: true`; under 20% it goes ahead and the answer carries a `warning`.

409.description: The app is being deleted, or the disk is almost full (`code: disk_critical`).

503.description: The job queue is not available.

400.description: The request was not valid. `error` says what is wrong; `details` lists each problem when there are several.

put.summary: Set the container paths to keep
put.description: Replaces the whole list. Each path becomes a Docker named volume that every deployment mounts, so files written there survive redeploys, rollbacks and restarts. A path that is new gets a new volume; a path that was removed earlier gets ITS volume back; a path that is left out is **detached, never deleted**. Takes effect with the next deployment (it is listed in `settings_pending`). The Docker volumes are created by the worker at deployment time, and a new version is first checked with throwaway volumes so the old version's data is not touched while both run.

400.description: A bad path, a duplicate, one path inside another, or more than 10.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

409.description: The app is being deleted (`code: deleting`).

get.description: The latest sign-in attempts and security changes, good and bad (names typed by strangers included), newest first. Kinds: `login`, `setup`, `recovery`, `reset` (a password reset on the machine), `settings` (public access changed), `github` (GitHub connected or changed).

get.description: The administrator's name; also a cheap way to check the session is still valid.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

get.description: Never the codes themselves: they exist in the clear only at the moment they are made.

post.summary: Make a new set of recovery codes
post.description: Replaces the whole set (the old codes stop working) and returns the ten new ones **once**. Needs the current password.

400.description: The request was not valid. `error` says what is wrong; `details` lists each problem when there are several.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

403.description: Refused: the Origin header is not one of Shipdok's own addresses, or the password given was wrong (`code: wrong_password`).

429.description: Too many tries. `Retry-After` and `retryAfterSeconds` say how long to wait.

get.summary: Is there an administrator, and is this browser signed in?
get.description: The first thing the dashboard asks. Safe to call without signing in. The setup token itself is never sent; `setupTokenRequired` only says whether the setup screen must ask for it.

Every build leaves layers in a cache that all apps share, so it belongs to no app and image clean-up does not touch it. The worker measures it every few minutes (the API never asks Docker), so `sampledAt` says how old the figure is. `last` is the most recent clean-up.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

get.description: The interactive reference built from this document (Scalar). A web page for the signed-in administrator, with everything served from Shipdok itself (no internet needed). Can be switched off with `API_DOCS=false`, in which case it answers 404.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

get.description: The OpenAPI 3.0 description of the API, as JSON. Generated from the code's route list and descriptions with `npm run openapi`.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

get.description: Scalar's browser bundle, served from Shipdok so the reference works without the internet. Used by the reference page.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

get.description: Every connected GitHub App, oldest first, never a secret, each with the projects assigned to it (`projects`, what the Disconnect warning lists). It also says what the webhook receiver refused lately for a wrong signature, from memory and with nothing but a number, a time and a count: `refusedPush` on the app whose secret did not match, and `unknownSenders` for pushes from an app that is not connected here. `problem: cannot_decrypt` on an app means its stored credentials do not fit the platform key; the others are not affected.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

get.summary: Does GitHub send this app's webhooks to the right address?
get.description: Compares the address GitHub has (read from that app) with the one Shipdok expects (the public address + `/api/webhooks/github`). Every GitHub app sends to the same Shipdok address; each has its own secret.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of a connected GitHub App (from `GET /api/github`).

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

409.description: That GitHub app's stored credentials cannot be read (`code: cannot_decrypt`).

get.description: For the branch pickers in the dashboard. With `app`, and when that GitHub App is installed on the repository, the branches are read with a token for that one repository (read-only); otherwise (no `app`, or it is not installed there) anonymously, which works for **public** repositories, and also when no GitHub App is connected at all. The default branch comes first, the rest alphabetical; at most the first 500 branches are read (`truncated`). Good answers are kept for a minute, separately for each GitHub app (what an app can see differs). A repository that is private and not covered by the app is a 404 `repo_not_found`; a GitHub rate limit is a 502 `rate_limited`.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: The id of the GitHub App to ask through. Left out: anonymously.

400.description: Not a repository name (`code: bad_repo`).

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

404.description: No such public repository, and the app is not installed on it (`code: repo_not_found`); or the `app` is not a connected GitHub App (`code: github_app_not_found`).

409.description: That GitHub app's credentials cannot be read (`code: cannot_decrypt`).

502.description: GitHub could not be reached (`github_unreachable`) or is limiting requests (`rate_limited`).

get.summary: Where GitHub sends the browser back
get.description: A page navigation, not an API call: GitHub redirects the browser here with a one-time `code` and the `state` from the start. Every outcome is a **302 redirect** to `/github?connected=<the new app's id>` or `/github?error=<login|state|exchange_failed|github_unreachable>`; the API trades the code for the app's credentials and stores them encrypted as one more GitHub App. The state is compared in constant time and used once whatever happens. No secret is ever put in a redirect.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The state returned by the start call.

302.description: Redirect to the GitHub page of the dashboard, with a short result code.

get.summary: Who may reach Shipdok from outside
get.description: The mode (`local`, `webhook` or `full`), the public address, whether the environment fixes either, and how THIS request was classified (`visitor`).

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

put.summary: Change who may reach Shipdok from outside
put.description: Needs the current password; takes effect at once; recorded in the sign-ins list. A value fixed by the environment (`SHIPDOK_PUBLIC`, `PUBLIC_URL`) cannot be changed here. The address is tidied to an origin (`https://host[:port]`, no path, no credentials). A new address is also sent to every connected GitHub app; the answer says how that went in `githubWebhook` (`failed` names the apps that did not take it; the setting is saved either way).

400.description: No password, nothing to change, a bad mode or a bad address.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

403.description: Wrong password, or the Origin is not allowed.

409.description: The environment fixes that setting (`code: locked_by_environment`).

get.description: Log bytes and image bytes per app (image sizes are upper bounds: versions of an app share layers), the persistent volumes as last measured (`volumes`; `0` and `measuredAt: null` until a measurement was asked for) and the disk's free space with a level: `ok`, `low` (under 20% free) or `critical` (under 10%).

get.summary: How the measuring of volume sizes stands
get.description: Whether a measurement is waiting or running, when the last one finished and how it went, the total of the last measured sizes and how many volumes have one. The sizes themselves are on each volume (`sizeBytes`, `measuredAt`).

post.summary: Measure the sizes of the persistent volumes
post.description: Asks the worker to add up every volume. Docker walks every file to do that, which takes seconds (longer for big volumes or a slow disk), so sizes are never measured by themselves. The API only records the request; the worker answers it beside the deployment queue, so it never holds a deployment up. Poll `GET /api/volumes/sizes` until `measuring` is false.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

409.description: One is already waiting or running (`code: already_measuring`).

get.description: The last 50 deliveries: "why didn't my push deploy?". `details` says, per app, what happened.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

get.description: Answers as long as the process runs (used by the container health check).
Like `/health`, and also checks that the database answers. Answers 503 while it does not.

post.description: All or nothing: if any line has a problem nothing is saved and `problems` lists them (up to 50) with their line numbers. Existing names are updated, new ones created, within the limit per app.

400.description: A problem in the file (`problems`, `total_problems`), no variables in it, or too many in total. Nothing was saved.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

post.description: The **only** place a value leaves the server. It is a POST so it is never prefetched or cached, and the answer says `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.summary: Roll back to an earlier version
post.description: Runs an earlier version's existing image again: nothing is cloned or built, so it works offline and needs no disk space. The new deployment (trigger `rollback`) uses the app's CURRENT settings and variables; only the image is old. Without `deploymentId` the newest earlier version that still has an image is used.

post.description: Sets the session cookie `shipdok.sid`. Failed tries are counted per name and per address: after five in a row the next ones are refused (429 `locked`) for 30 seconds, doubling, up to 15 minutes per name and 60 per address. While locked even the right password is refused.

400.description: Username or password missing.

401.description: Wrong name or password (the same answer for an unknown name).

429.description: Locked for a while; see the description.

post.description: Ends this session and clears the cookie.

post.summary: Sign out every browser and device
post.description: Ends every session of the administrator, this one included.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

post.description: Needs a session AND the current password. Every other session ends and this one gets a new id. A wrong current password is a **403** (`wrong_password`), not a 401, so a client does not mistake it for an ended session. Limited to 10 tries per 15 minutes.

400.description: Missing fields, a weak new password (`code: weak_password`), or the same as the current one.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

403.description: The current password is wrong (`code: wrong_password`) or the Origin is not allowed.

newPassword.description: Must pass the password rules and differ from the current one.

post.summary: Set a new password with a recovery code
post.description: For a lost password: the name, one recovery code and a new password. A weak new password is refused BEFORE the code is looked at, so that answer says nothing about the code and does not use it up. A good code is spent (single use), the password is set, every session ends and this browser is signed in. Wrong code, used code and unknown name all give the same 401. Tries share the sign-in lockout.

200.description: Signed in with the new password.

400.description: Missing fields, or the new password does not pass the rules (`code: weak_password`).

401.description: Wrong name or code.

code.description: A recovery code; case, spaces and dashes do not matter.

post.description: Creates the one administrator account, signs this browser in, and returns the ten recovery codes **once**. Works only while no administrator exists (a second call is 409). While the platform has a setup token (printed in the API log), it must be sent as `setupToken`. The password must pass the password rules.

400.description: The name or the password does not pass the rules (`error` says which).

403.description: The setup token is missing or wrong.

409.description: An administrator already exists.

429.description: Too many tries from this address.

setupToken.description: The setup token from the API log; needed while `setupTokenRequired` is true.

post.description: Queues the clean-up on the same queue as deployments, so it never runs during a build. It removes build cache only: no images, containers, volumes or logs. By default it keeps what a build used in the last 24 hours; `all: true` removes every unused entry and the next builds start from nothing (slow). Only one clean-up at a time.

400.description: Invalid body.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

409.description: One is already waiting or running (`code: already_queued`).

503.description: The job queue is not available.

post.description: A queued deployment ends at once (200). A running one is only asked to stop (202); the worker stops it and the final status appears after clean-up. A deployment already past the swap point finishes.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

409.description: It has already finished.

post.summary: Enter an existing GitHub App by hand
post.description: Adds a GitHub App (there is no limit on how many). The key and id are proven with GitHub (`GET /app`) BEFORE anything is stored, so a typo never adds or replaces anything. Entering a GitHub App that is already connected replaces its credentials (same `id`, answer 200, `created: false`; its projects and their installations are kept, because the installations belong to the same GitHub App). Needs the current password. Recorded in the sign-ins list as a GitHub change.

200.description: The same GitHub App was already connected: its credentials were replaced.

400.description: A missing or malformed field, or GitHub did not accept the id and key (`code: github_rejected`), or the key belongs to another app (`code: app_id_mismatch`).

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

403.description: Wrong password, or the Origin is not allowed.

502.description: GitHub could not be reached (`code: github_unreachable`) or could not check the app.

post.summary: Point one GitHub App at the right webhook address
post.description: Updates only the address on GitHub (never the secret), for that app. The retry for the automatic update, which follows a change of the public address and tells every connected app.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of a connected GitHub App (from `GET /api/github`).

400.description: No public address is set yet (`code: no_public_address`).

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

409.description: That GitHub app's stored credentials cannot be read (`code: cannot_decrypt`).

502.description: GitHub could not be reached or did not accept it.

post.description: Returns a prepared GitHub App definition (`manifest`) and the address (`postUrl`, always on github.com) the browser posts it to. Each run adds one more GitHub App, whether or not others are connected. Keeps a one-time `state` in the session for 10 minutes. The manifest asks only for read access to contents and metadata and the push event, and the app is created private. Needs an Origin that is one of the dashboard's own addresses, because GitHub sends the browser back there.

400.description: A bad name or organisation, or the dashboard was not opened at its own address.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

post.description: Called by GitHub, not by people. **Public and protected only by the HMAC signature** (`X-Hub-Signature-256`, SHA-256 over the exact bytes, compared in constant time). Order: size limit, signature, shape, then the database. A push to a branch that an app tracks deploys that app (every app tracking the repository and branch); other events and branches are recorded and ignored. Deliveries are deduplicated by `X-GitHub-Delivery`. Pushes are not built while the disk is critically full. Rate limited to 120 requests a minute per client. Answers 503 until a GitHub App is connected. Which visitors can reach it from outside depends on the public access mode.

parameters.name: X-Hub-Signature-256
parameters.description: `sha256=` and the hex HMAC of the body, with the webhook secret.

400.description: A missing or invalid header, or the payload is not a JSON object.

401.description: The signature is missing or wrong.

503.description: No GitHub App is connected (`Webhooks are not configured`), or the queue is unavailable.

requestBody.description: GitHub's JSON payload (set the webhook content type to `application/json`).

put.summary: Set how many versions to keep
put.description: How many earlier versions' images to keep besides the live one (0 to 10), and whether to clean up automatically after each successful deployment. Send either or both.

400.description: Invalid settings.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session ended (30 minutes without activity, or 12 hours in all).

409.description: The app is being deleted (`code: deleting`): it accepts nothing but another delete.

session.name: shipdok.sid
session.description: The administrator's session cookie, set by `POST /api/auth/login`.

code.description: A short stable code for programs, where there is one (for example `wrong_password`, `locked`, `port_taken`).

details.description: Each problem, when a request had several.

AppCreate.description: A new app. `host_port` left out: the lowest free port in the platform's port range is used.

AppUpdate.description: Settings to change; send only the ones you want to change. The repository and the slug cannot be changed.

Retention.description: How many earlier versions' images to keep, and whether to clean up automatically.

RollbackRequest.description: `deploymentId`: the version to go back to (default: the newest earlier version that still has an image). `start`: also start the app if it is stopped.

DeployRequest.description: `start`: start the app after deploying if it is stopped. `ignoreDiskWarning`: deploy although the disk is almost full. `noCache`: build this one deployment without Docker's build cache (every step runs again; slower).

Runtime.description: What the worker last reported about the running container. `null` (on the app) until it has reported.

state.description: What the worker last saw. `missing`: the container was removed outside Shipdok.

last_action.description: The last thing the worker did.

last_error.description: Why the last action or the current state is a problem.

last_exit_code.description: The exit code of the last time the container stopped.

oom_killed.description: Whether that stop was an out-of-memory kill.

health_failures.description: Health checks failed in a row.

next_restart_at.description: When a scheduled automatic restart is due.

Stats.description: The newest CPU and memory reading of the running container, or `null` when it is older than 90 seconds (the app is stopped or the worker is quiet).

cpuPercent.description: A share of ONE processor, like `docker stats`; above 100 when more than one is busy. `null` when there is nothing to compare with yet.

memoryBytes.description: Memory in use, without the file cache the kernel can take back.

Cleanup.description: What the last image clean-up of the app did (`null` until one has run).

freed_bytes.description: Disk space freed, measured as the drop in Docker's layer usage (0 if Docker cannot say).

skipped.description: Images that were not removed because something still uses them.

error.description: A failure, if there was one.

RunningSettings.description: The settings the running version was deployed with (the newest successful deployment's snapshot, without variable versions). `null` until one succeeded. Editing the app changes the NEXT deployment, not this.

slug.description: Normalised name; names the images and containers and never changes.

github_installation_id.description: The GitHub App installation remembered for this repository (`null` until found).

github_app_id.description: The connected GitHub App this project uses to list and clone its repository and whose webhooks deploy it (`null`: none, for a public repository deployed by hand).

root_dir.description: Where the Dockerfile is, inside the repository.

container_port.description: The port the app listens on inside its container.

host_port.description: The port it is published on, on this machine.

health_path.description: A path that answers when the app is healthy (`null`: any answer counts).

cpus.description: CPU limit, as a decimal string (for example `"1.00"`).

max_restarts.description: Automatic restarts allowed within 10 minutes before the app is marked crashed.

build_timeout_minutes.description: Minutes the clone and the build may take before they are stopped (5 to 10080); `null` = no limit (the default). A build that hangs and has no limit blocks the queue until it is cancelled.

build_method.description: How the image is made: `dockerfile` builds the repository's own Dockerfile (the default); `railpack` needs no Dockerfile: Railpack looks at the code, works out how to build it and Shipdok builds that plan, even when the repository has a Dockerfile.

install_command.description: Railpack only: replaces its install step (for example `npm ci`). `null`: Railpack decides. A custom one replaces the default entirely. Kept when the method is switched back to `dockerfile`.

build_command.description: Railpack only: replaces its build step. `null`: Railpack decides.

start_command.description: Railpack only: the command that starts the app. `null`: Railpack decides. The app is given `PORT` (the container port) to listen on.

desired_state.description: What the administrator wants. What really happens is in `runtime`.

keep_previous_images.description: Earlier versions' images kept besides the running one.

auto_prune.description: Clean up images automatically after each successful deployment.

deleting_at.description: Set while the app is being deleted.

delete_error.description: Why a deletion failed (press delete again to retry).

settings_pending.description: Only on the single-app answers: which edited settings the running version does not have yet, including `volumes` for persistent storage (`null`: nothing deployed yet).

warning.description: Only when creating: for example that the GitHub App is not installed on the repository.

DeploymentStatus.description: Where a deployment is. Separate from whether the app is running.

image_ref.description: The Docker image built or reused.

image_bytes.description: Image size in bytes, as a string.

image_removed_at.description: When the image was cleaned up (the version can no longer be rolled back to).

rollback_of.description: For a rollback: the version it went back to.

config_snapshot.description: The settings this deployment used (no secret values).

error_summary.description: A short reason it failed; the build log has the detail.

superseded_by.description: The newer deployment that replaced it.

warning.description: Only when requesting: for example that the disk is getting full.

cause.description: Why the app was not running when it should be.

exit_code.description: The exit code, where there was one.

oom_killed.description: Killed for running out of memory.

state.description: live: runs now. previous: kept for rollback. prunable: a clean-up would remove it. removed: its image is gone.

canRollBackTo.description: Whether Roll back can use it.

prunableBytes.description: What a clean-up would free (an upper bound).

path.description: The container path it is mounted at.

state.description: in_use: listed for the app and mounted by its deployments. detached: the path was removed from the list; the data is KEPT but not mounted. orphaned: the app was deleted and its data kept.

dockerName.description: The Docker volume name (`shipdok-vol-<id>`), for example for a manual backup.

appId.description: The app, or `null` once it is gone.

appName.description: The app's name (remembered after the app is deleted).

removeError.description: Why the last request to delete it did not work.

sizeBytes.description: Its size at the last measurement (`POST /api/volumes/sizes`), or `null` if it was never measured or Docker has no such volume yet.

measuring.description: A measurement was asked for and has not finished (an unanswered request stops counting after 30 minutes).

error.description: Why the last one failed, in plain words.

totalBytes.description: The sum of every volume's last measured size.

measured.description: How many volumes have a measured size.

paths.description: The container paths to keep (absolute; letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore, slash; not `/`, not under `/proc`, `/sys` or `/dev`; no duplicates and none inside another). The whole list: a path that is left out is detached, never deleted.

BranchList.description: The default branch first, the rest in alphabetical order.

defaultBranch.description: The repository's default branch (`null` if GitHub did not say).

truncated.description: There were more branches than the first 500 that were read.

totalBytes.description: Size of Docker's build cache when the worker last measured it (`null` until it has, or if this Docker cannot say).

reclaimableBytes.description: The part no build is using, which a clean-up can remove.

cleaning.description: A clean-up was asked for and has not reported back yet.

all.description: It removed every unused entry (otherwise only those unused for a day).

error.description: Why it failed, if it did.

all.description: `true`: remove every unused entry, so the next builds start from nothing. Default `false`: only cache no build has used for 24 hours.

value.description: Always `********`: values are never returned here.

scope.description: Where it is available: the running container, `docker build` only, or both.

build_as.description: How a variable that reaches the build is given to `docker build`: a build argument (`arg`) or a BuildKit secret (`secret`). Means nothing for `runtime`.

deployed.description: Whether the app has been deployed.

pending.description: Whether any change waits for the next deployment.

offset.description: Byte offset of the start of `text`.

complete.description: The log has finished AND everything has been read.

truncated.description: The log hit its size cap.

deploymentId.description: Runtime logs only: the deployment whose container wrote it.

Disk.description: The disk the logs (and normally Docker) live on, or `null` if it cannot be measured.

level.description: low: under 20% free. critical: under 10% free.

totalBytes.description: Every persistent volume as last measured (including those whose app is gone). `0` until a measurement was made.

measured.description: How many have a measured size.

username.description: 3 to 64 characters: letters, numbers, dot, dash, underscore.

password.description: 12 to 256 characters; refused: a repeated short pattern, a plain run of characters, or one containing the username.

authenticated.description: This browser has a valid session.

setupTokenRequired.description: The setup screen must ask for the setup token (the token is printed in the API log).

SetupResult.description: The only time the recovery codes are ever returned.

username.description: The name typed (any name, real or not).

address.description: The client address (`host` for a reset on the machine).

createdAt.description: When the current set was made.

mode.description: Who may reach Shipdok from outside.

publicUrl.description: The public address (an origin, no path), or `null`.

githubWebhook.description: Only after a change of the public address while a GitHub app is connected.

updated.description: Whether every connected GitHub app now has the new webhook address.

failed.description: The names of the GitHub apps that did not take it.

GithubApp.description: A connected GitHub App. Never contains a secret.

id.description: Shipdok's id for this GitHub App (what a project's `github_app_id` refers to).

problem.description: `cannot_decrypt`: the stored credentials do not fit the platform key.

refusedPush.description: Set when a push that GitHub says this app sent was refused lately because its signature did not match the stored webhook secret. Gone after a day, after a good delivery from this app, or when its credentials are entered again. Kept in memory: also gone when the API restarts.

at.description: When the newest one was refused.

projects.description: The projects assigned to this GitHub App.

apps.description: Every connected GitHub App, oldest first.

unknownSenders.description: Pushes refused lately because they were signed by nothing Shipdok has: from a GitHub App that is not connected here (`appNumber` is its number) or that did not say which app it was (`appNumber` is `null`). Newest first, kept in memory for a day or until that app is connected.

appNumber.description: GitHub's number for the sending app (digits), or `null`.

at.description: When the newest one was refused.

created.description: `true` for a new GitHub App, `false` when an app that was already connected had its credentials replaced.

appId.description: The App ID (a number; not the Client ID).

webhookSecret.description: The app's webhook secret, 16 to 256 characters.

account.description: The account it is installed on.
